title: Protocol for the assessment of mTOR activity in mouse primary hepatocytes
protocol: Warm the Perfusion Solution and the Digestion Solution in a water bath at 37°C.
Add collagenase to the Digestion Solution immediately before starting the isolation procedure.
Anesthetize the mouse according to your institution’s approved animal protocol.
Perform two surgical knots in the abdominal and thoracic cavities of the anesthetized mouse.
Cannulate the heart through the left atrium.
Perfuse and digest the liver in situ using the warmed Perfusion Solution and Digestion Solution.
Confirm that the mouse is completely anesthetized before continuing.
Wash the perfusion line extensively with Rinsing Solution to eliminate 70% ethanol.
Place one end of the perfusion line inside the Perfusion Solution located inside the water bath.
Fill the perfusion line with Perfusion Solution before opening the mouse peritoneal cavity.
Connect the outlet end of the perfusion line to the catheter.
Immobilize the anesthetized mouse by using needles to attach the upper and lower limbs on a dissecting board.
Spray the mouse with 70% ethanol to ease dissection.
Open the abdominal cavity with surgical scissors and forceps.
Carefully lean the small intestine to expose the inferior vena cava and portal vein.
Add approximately 2 mL of Rising Solution into the abdominal cavity using a syringe to prevent contaminations.
Pass the needle under the inferior vena cava and the left kidney, located at the researcher’s right side.
Pass the needle above the kidney located at the researcher’s left side.
Tie a loose knot for stable liver perfusion.
Thoracic knot: Open the thoracic cavity vertically cutting the ribs on both sides.
Remove the ribs to facilitate posterior cannulation.
Pass the needle under the visible aorta artery above the liver and tie a loose knot.
Make an incision in the left atrium of the heart and cannulate.
Switch on the pump to begin a very slow perfusion (1 mL/min) of the mouse liver with Perfusion Solution.
Secure the catheter with two needles.
Tighten the thoracic knot to secure the catheter above the liver.
Tighten the abdominal knot below the liver.
Cut the inferior vena cava below the knot.
Wait until the portal vein becomes distended, and then cut the portal vein.
Verify that no bubbles are introduced during cannulation.
Perfuse approximately 25 mL of Perfusion Solution at a rate of 5 mL/min.
Switch the end of the perfusion line from Perfusion Solution to Digestion Solution.
Perfuse the liver with 25 mL of Digestion Solution at a rate of 3.5 mL/min.
Briefly turn off the perfusion pump when switching from Perfusion Solution to Digestion Solution to avoid bubbles.
Collect mouse liver carefully after perfusion with Digestion Solution.
Remove gallbladder and tissue leftovers from diaphragm.
Transfer liver to 25 mL of Hepatocyte Attachment Medium in a 50 mL centrifuge tube on ice.
Place the 50 mL tube containing the liver in a shaker for 5 min on ice to facilitate hepatocyte release.
Wash the perfusion line of the pump with Rinsing Solution after liver perfusion of one mouse.
Filter the mouse liver through a 100 μm cell strainer, transferring the sample to a clean 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Gently smash the liver with the plunger of a 10 ml syringe on top of the cell strainer for disaggregation.
Use 10 ml extra of Hepatocyte Attachment Medium to clean the initial centrifuge tube and recover possible remaining cells.
Centrifuge the filtered hepatocytes at 50 × g for 5 min at 20ºC–25ºC.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellets with 25 mL of Hepatocyte Attachment Medium.
Add 25 mL of Gradient Solution slowly to the resuspended cells without mixing.
Homogenize the solution by flipping the centrifuge tube 10 times.
Centrifuge at 50 × g for 10 min at 20ºC–25ºC with deceleration.
Centrifuge the hepatocytes to remove dead cells.
Aspirate the supernatant carefully to remove dead cells.
Resuspend the pellet using 20 mL of Hepatocyte Attachment Medium.
Centrifuge the cells at 50 × g for 5 min at 20°C–25°C.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the pellet with Hepatocyte Attachment Medium.
Gently homogenize the hepatocyte suspension by pipetting up and down with a 1000 μL pipette.
Stain the hepatocytes with 10 μL of cell sample with 10 μL of Trypan Blue staining solution.
Count both dead (dark blue) and live (translucent) cells using a TC20 Automated cell counter to calculate the survival rate.
Plate 300,000 live hepatocytes per well in the collagen-coated 6 multi-well plates with 2 ml of Hepatocyte Attachment Medium.
Replace the medium after 6 h and culture hepatocytes for another 16 h with Hepatocyte Attachment Medium before the signaling experiment.
Plate liver cells at a confluence of 300,000 hepatocytes per 3.5 cm well for signaling experiments.
Wash each well with Rinsing Solution 6 hours after plating to prevent potential contaminations before changing the medium.
Rinse cultured hepatocytes three times with Pre-starvation Medium.
Aspirate thoroughly the medium in each wash to remove any leftover of the Hepatocyte Attachment Medium.
Add 2 mL of Amino acid Starvation Medium to each well.
Return the plates to the incubator for 1 h.
Incubate hepatocytes in Amino acid Starvation Medium for 1 hour.
Add 200 μL of amino acids cocktail to the treatment group wells.
Add 200 μL of amino acid Starvation Medium (without amino acids) to control, non-replenished hepatocytes.
Replace medium with 2 mL Hepatocyte Attachment Medium after 16 hours for high mTORC1 activity condition.
Place cell plates on ice once timepoints are finished.
Wash cells twice with cold PBS.
Aspirate thoroughly the PBS in each wash.
Add 150 μL of cold, freshly prepared Protein Lysis Buffer to each well of the plate.
Scrape hepatocytes with cell lifters and collect them in 1.5 mL centrifuge tubes.
Incubate the samples at 4°C for 10 minutes with rotation in the ELMI Intelli Mixer.
Centrifuge the samples at 4°C for 10 minutes at 21,130 g.
Transfer the supernatant to a new 1.5 mL centrifuge tube.
Quantify protein concentration using the Pierce BCA method or an equivalent method.
Load 8 μg of protein in each lane on a 16% polyacrylamide gel.
Run and transfer a standard Western Blot.
Probe for levels of Phospho-Thr389-p70 S6 Kinase (1:500).
Probe for total S6 Kinase (1:500).
Probe for levels of Phospho-Ser235/236-S6 (1:1000).
Probe for total S6 (1:1000).
Probe for levels of Phospho-Thr37/46-4E-BP1 (1:500).
Probe for total 4E-BP1 (1:500).
Change medium: Replace the medium (Hepatocyte Attachment Medium) 16–24 h after plating.
Rinse cultured hepatocytes three times with FBS withdrawal Medium.
Thoroughly aspirate the medium in each wash to remove any leftover of FBS from the Hepatocyte Attachment Medium.
Add 2 ml of FBS withdrawal Medium to each well.
Return the plates to the incubator and leave for 16 h.
Add 2 μL of 100 μM insulin to the corresponding wells after 16 h.
Wash hepatocytes twice with cold PBS.
Aspirate thoroughly the PBS in each wash for minimal leftover volume.
Add 150 μL of Protein Lysis Buffer to each well of the plate.
Collect hepatocytes with cell lifters in 1.5 mL centrifuge tubes.
Incubate samples at 4°C during 10 min with rotation in the ELMI Intelli Mixer.
Centrifuge at 4°C during 10 min at 21,130 g.
Transfer supernatant to a new 1.5 mL centrifuge tube.
Quantify protein concentration with Pierce BCA method.
Load 8 μg of protein in each lane in a 16% polyacrylamide gel.
Proceed to run the Western Blot.
Transfer the proteins from the gel to a membrane.
Probe for levels of Phospho-Thr389-p70 S6 Kinase (1:500).
Probe for total S6 Kinase (1:500).
Probe for Phospho-Ser235/236-S6 (1:1000).
Probe for total S6 (1:1000).
Probe for Phospho-Thr37/46-4E-BP1 (1:500).
Probe for total 4E-BP1 (1:1000).
Probe for Phospho-Ser473-Akt (1:1000).
Probe for total Akt (1:1000).
